turns.prompt_text: Onlington.com. Is there a way I can download all the messages I've received.
turns.response_html:
Based on current information, Onlington.com does not appear to have a standard, publicly documented "Export All Messages" button in its user interface.

If you are looking to save your communications from the platform, here are the best ways

Yes, LinkedIn has a built-in feature that allows you to download a copy of all your messages, along with other account data.

Here is the step-by-step guide to doing it on a desktop:

1. Request Your Data Archive

  1. Click the Me icon at the top of your LinkedIn homepage.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy from the dropdown menu.
  3. Click Data Privacy on the left-hand sidebar.
  4. In the "How LinkedIn uses your data" section, click Get a copy of your data.
  5. You have two options here:
    • Download larger data archive: This includes everything (posts, activity, etc.) and can take up to 24–48 hours.
    • Want something in particular? Select this and check the box for Messages. This is usually much faster (often ready within 10–15 minutes).
  6. Click Request archive. You may be asked to re-enter your password for security.

2. Download the File

  1. LinkedIn will send an email to your primary address when the download is ready.
  2. Go back to the same Get a copy of your data page in your settings.
  3. Click the Download archive button. It will download as a .zip file.
  4. Once you unzip the file, look for a file named messages.csv. You can open this file with Excel, Google Sheets, or any text editor to see a complete log of your sent and received messages.

Important Tips

  • Time Limit: The download link is only active for 72 hours. If you miss it, you'll have to request it again.
  • Desktop Only: This feature is generally not available on the mobile app; you should use a desktop or laptop browser.
  • Media/Images: If you want images or attachments sent in messages, these are usually included in a separate "Rich Media" folder within the larger data export.

If you are looking for a way to automatically sync messages to a CRM or a spreadsheet on an ongoing basis, you would likely need a third-party tool (like PhantomBuster or a CRM integration), as LinkedIn's native tool is a one-time manual export.

turns.prompt_text: And you download my data section. I only see options for articles recommendations invitations registration. and profile
turns.response_html:
If you don't see "Messages" as an individual checkbox under the "Something in particular" section, it is usually due to one of three reasons.

Here is how to find your messages based on current LinkedIn interface behavior:

1. Check the "Large Archive" Option

LinkedIn sometimes moves specific data points (like Messages and Connections) out of the "quick" list and bundles them into the larger file to prevent frequent scraping.

  • Instead of selecting "Want something in particular," select the top option: "Download larger data archive, including connections, contacts, account history..."
  • This will definitely include your messages, though it takes longer to process (usually between 24 and 48 hours).

2. The "Hidden" Scroll or Page Bug

Sometimes the list of checkboxes is longer than it appears, or the "Messages" option is listed under a name like "Communications" or "Messaging." * Try zooming out in your browser ($Ctrl$ + $-$ or $Cmd$ + $-$) to see if more checkboxes appear.

  • If you still only see Articles, Recommendations, Invitations, Registration, and Profile, your account may be restricted from "quick" exports, and you must use the Large Archive option mentioned above.

3. Check for a Pending Request

If you recently clicked "Request Archive" for a different set of data, LinkedIn will not show you the full list of options again until that first request is finished or has expired.

  • Look for a message on that same page that says "Request Pending" or "Download available." * You may need to wait for that to clear or download that file first to see the full menu again.

What to do next:

If you need those messages urgently, I recommend requesting the "Large Data Archive" right now. Even though it says "24 hours," it often arrives much faster (sometimes in 3–4 hours).

Once you get the file:

  1. Download the .zip folder.
  2. Open the folder and look for the file named messages.csv.
  3. Open that file in Excel or Google Sheets; it will show you the sender, the recipient, the date, and the full text of every message.
